chain.label: Attendance policy penalized fatigue calls
chain.trigger: Shuttle America's failure to administer an attendance policy that permitted flight crewmembers to call in as fatigued without fear of reprisals

chain.label: Captain severely sleep-deprived at the controls
chain.trigger: the captain reported that he was unable to sleep that night, stating that he received only 45 minutes to 1 hour of sleep; he had been awake for all but about 1 hour of the previous 32 hours

caused_by.evidence: The captain did not advise Shuttle America of his fatigue or remove himself from duty because he thought he would be terminated if he took this action.

chain.label: Short snow-contaminated runway 28, braking action fair
chain.trigger: Runway 28 ... was 6,017 feet long ... the braking action was 'fair'; reported conditions were 1/2-inch cover of snow over scattered thin patches of compacted snow

chain.label: Rapidly deteriorating heavy snow, RVR falling below minimums
chain.trigger: the weather conditions had rapidly deteriorated while the airplane was on approach, with moderate to heavy snow reported during the approach and at the time of the landing; the runway 28 RVR fell from 6,000 to 2,000 feet

chain.label: Approach preparation and briefing omissions
chain.trigger: both pilots indicated that they had not read this NOTAM ... The first officer did not brief the runway length, and the captain did not request this information

caused_by.evidence: Before the flight, the captain did not adequately review the flight release paperwork, which would have provided him with an early warning of the glideslope status at CLE.

chain.label: Crew flew approach to ILS DH instead of localizer MDA
chain.trigger: Because the flight crewmembers assumed that the glideslope was working properly, they used the ILS decision height (DH), which was 227 feet agl, instead of the localizer (glideslope out) minimum descent altitude (MDA), which was 429 feet agl

caused_by.evidence: Neither flight crewmember discussed the information in each ATIS broadcast about the unusable glideslopes.
Although he and the first officer were confused when the approach controller told them that the glideslope was unusable, the captain allowed the precision approach to continue to ILS minimums.

chain.label: Missed approach not executed although runway not distinctly visible
chain.trigger: the failure of the flight crew to execute a missed approach when visual cues for the runway were not distinct and identifiable; the captain stated 'let's go [around]' but the first officer continued the approach

caused_by.evidence: the flight crewmembers would have been required to execute a missed approach if they had been using the localizer (glideslope out) approach. The MDA ... was 429 feet agl. No CVR evidence ... indicated that either crewmember had the runway environment in sight by that altitude.
when the airplane was 10 feet agl, he momentarily lost sight of the runway because a snow squall came through and he 'could not see anything.'

When he lost visibility after descending through the DH, the captain did not reinforce his go-around callout or respond otherwise after the first officer did not execute the missed approach, as instructed.

chain.label: Long landing 2,900 feet down the runway
chain.trigger: the airplane touched down about 2,900 feet down the 6,017-foot runway

caused_by.evidence: because the first officer lost sight of the runway just before landing, he should have abandoned the landing attempt and immediately executed a missed approach
the airplane touched down farther rather than closer to the threshold likely because the airplane floated for some distance

chain.label: Crew unaware of actual touchdown point and remaining runway
chain.trigger: the captain stated that he thought the airplane had touched down closer to the runway threshold, and the first officer stated that, during the landing rollout, he could not see the end of the runway or any distance remaining signs

caused_by.evidence: he could not see the end of the runway or any distance remaining signs (which appeared every 1,000 feet)
it is unlikely that the flight crew would have seen the 3,000-foot distance remaining sign

chain.label: Reverse thrust and wheel braking not used to maximum effectiveness
chain.trigger: engine reverse thrust reached a peak of only 65 percent N1 ... for about 2 seconds before the commanded reverse thrust tapered off to reverse idle; the first officer's initial wheel brake application was about 20 percent of maximum

caused_by.evidence: the results of the aircraft performance study showed that reverse idle thrust had been commanded well before a safe stop could be ensured ... only light wheel braking was applied early in the landing rollout
The captain did not continuously monitor the first officer's landing actions, including the touchdown point, use of thrust reverse, and braking application.

chain.label: Substandard 60-foot runway safety area with antenna and fence beyond
chain.trigger: The runway 28 departure end had an RSA that was 60 feet long and 275 feet wide ... a fence, runway edge identifier lights, a localizer, a localizer building

chain.label: Airplane overran departure end of runway 28
chain.trigger: Airplane departed runway. Groundspeed was about 42 knots.

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's touchdown at 2,900 feet down the 6,017-foot runway was an unacceptably long landing
The flight crewmembers did not use reverse thrust and braking to their maximum effectiveness; if they had done so, the airplane would likely have stopped before the end of the runway.
braking effectiveness on contaminated runways is reduced because of low tire-to-runway friction

chain.label: Struck ILS antenna and perimeter fence; nose gear collapsed
chain.trigger: it overran the end of the runway, contacted an instrument landing system antenna, and struck an airport perimeter fence. The airplane's nose gear collapsed during the overrun.

caused_by.evidence: The airplane came to rest on a snow-covered grass surface located southwest of the extended runway 28 centerline.
the airplane would have traveled 127 feet into the arrestor bed before stopping (for a total of 162 feet beyond the runway threshold)

chain.label: Three passengers minor injuries; airplane substantially damaged
chain.trigger: 3 passengers received minor injuries. The airplane received substantial damage from impact forces.

caused_by.evidence: The airplane's nose landing gear, right wing leading edge ... and both engine nacelles received substantial damage from the impact forces.
